README Expected outcomes — E2E-19. The contract is the ABSENCE of a `XX%` confidence badge on a fresh install, which mustNotContain cannot express because the number varies — hence mustNotMatch.

The pattern asserts the BADGE SHAPE, not any percentage. The badge has exactly one render site, comment-formatter.ts:423 — ``` ` ${f.confidence}% ` ``` — so it is always backtick-wrapped, and matching on that is both precise and cheap.

It used to be a bare `\\d{1,3}%` with a negative lookahead excluding `%` followed by two hex digits, to dodge the percent-encoded View-full-details link (`mergewatch%2Ffixtures%3A3110%23…`). The lookahead did that correctly and is NOT needed once the backticks are required — do not re-add it, it only ever compensated for the imprecision of matching bare percentages.

What the lookahead never guarded was model prose. On mergewatch/mergewatch.ai@45fc2c3 this fixture failed the deploy gate on the orchestrator's own sentence — "does not meet the 75% confidence threshold for reporting" — and blocked production on a comment-formatter change that emits no percentages at all. A review about confidence filtering is exactly the review most likely to say "confidence threshold". See mergewatch/fixtures#3259.

One-sided with respect to the FEATURE: it can only fail if the confidence default flips back on. It is not one-sided with respect to the model — the previous note claimed it was, and that claim is what made the failure surprising.
